item.title: Steelers expected to release Aaron Rodgers after crazy Pat McAfee interview
item.description: Steelers expected to release Aaron Rodgers after crazy Pat McAfee interview originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers lost to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, and all sorts of problems have come from that. Aaron Rodgers was shockingly benched on Tuesday night before a Friday game against the Denver Broncos . But the next day, Rodgers went on to The Pat McAfee Show and unloaded on the Steelers, and specifically, head coach Mike McCarthy. It was an inflammatory interview, and it's spurred the Steelers to make a decision. According to Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette , the Steelers are expected to release Rodgers. Following his interview, the Steelers have seemingly seen more than enough and are cutting ties with the veteran quarterback. Steelers expected to cut Aaron Rodgers after crazy interview "SOURCES: Steelers are expected to release quarterback Aaron Rodgers, a decision that was hastened when Rodgers went on Pat McAfee and accused Mike McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings and saying the whole team knows something is physically wrong with the 63-year-old coach," Dulac reports. This report from Dulac shouldn't come as a surprise, as the things that Rodgers said during his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show are not something that could ever be recovered from. The Rodgers and Steelers relationship was over once that interview began, and the only question was about how things would go from there. Well, the Steelers have seemingly made their decision to cut ties with Rodgers, the future Hall of Fame quarterback playing in his final NFL season. Rodgers will have finished his 2026 NFL season with the Steelers going 6-4 with 2,241 passing yards, 16 passing touchdowns, and four interceptions in 10 starts. Mason Rudolph will be the starting quarterback going forward, with Drew Allar and Will Howard as depth options, with a bit more upside waiting on the bench. item.title: Patriots Quickly Emerge as Favorite to Acquire Aaron Rodgers
item.description: Aaron Rodgers’ days with the Pittsburgh Steelers appear to be over. Following the team’s decision to bench him on Tuesday night, the future Hall of Fame quarterback made an appearance on the “Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday. During that interview with Pat McAfee, Rodgers did not hold back from sharing the details leading up to his release. Rodgers shared that head coach Mike McCarthy was falling asleep during and missing team meetings. He revealed that he had met with McCarthy and urged him to give up play-calling. Obviously, those meetings did not conclude with the star quarterback’s desired outcome. Instead, the four-time NFL MVP has been benched. He is clearly hoping to be released by the Steelers. Whether or not the team will accommodate him remains unknown. Should Rodgers end up becoming a free agent, there are a few teams who could have interest. The New England Patriots are the team who has quickly emerged as the favorite to acquire the 42-year-old signal caller. New England makes perfect sense. Drake Maye suffered a serious injury and could miss the rest of the season. With Tommy DeVito as the starter, the Patriots have been struggling. Mike Vrabel and company have lost two straight games and currently hold a 5-5 record. Even at this stage of his career, Rodgers would be a massive upgrade over DeVito. So far this season in Pittsburgh, Rodgers has played in 10 games. He has completed 60.9 percent of his pass attempts for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions. Those numbers may not be the former MVP version of Rodgers. But, they’re still quality numbers. If Rodgers is released, it would be no surprise to see him quickly end up with the Patriots as their new starting quarterback. item.title: Max Verstappen’s F1 Weekend – Las Vegas GP Win and 40 Hours of GTA VI
item.description: Max Verstappen won the F1 Las Vegas GP after spending about 40 hours playing GTA VI during the race weekend, he said on a livestream. At the start of the F1 Las Vegas GP weekend on Wednesday, Red Bull ’s Verstappen confirmed that he had downloaded the most-awaited GTA VI from Rockstar Games. He was one of several drivers waiting to play the PlayStation game. Not much was said throughout the F1 weekend about whether he played or not, considering he was busy in his latest spat with Mercedes’ George Russell from FP3 onward. The Brit did what he did to stand up against the Dutchman. Verstappen responded after winning the F1 Las Vegas GP that he saw Russell to be below him and that Russell’s off was karma. Having returned home before the trip to this weekend’s Qatar GP, the Dutchman streamed with Team Redline. Verstappen Wins Las Vegas GP After Marathon GTA VI Max Verstappen celebrates winning the Las Vegas GP. Image Credit: Clive Rose/Getty Images During the stream, he was asked if he played GTA VI on his jet returning home. But Verstappen revealed he spent about 40 hours on the game during the Las Vegas GP weekend, dovetailing the racing and playing the game. “Good question. Maybe 40? (40 hours?) Yes,” said Verstappen to his fellow streamer. “No, no, I was just sleeping on the plane. I played a lot, at night and in the morning in Las Vegas,” summed up Verstappen, highlighting his mental strength. Having spent so many hours in front of the screen, Verstappen still managed to qualify in the Top 3 and fight against Russell, Isack Hadjar and Andrea Kimi Antonelli to win the F1 Las Vegas GP – which was a slipstream fest, with 35 lead changes. Norris Was Not Allowed to Play GTA As a Kid Lando Norris celebrates pole position at Interlagos. Image Credit: Steven Tee/LAT Images via Getty Images Among others to play was teammate Hadjar, who tried it after the launch. Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton was excited to play, along with Charles Leclerc and Antonelli. McLaren’s Lando Norris, meanwhile, turned down the offer with no interest. He shared that as a kid he wasn’t allowed to play GTA, which is why he had little interest. “I don’t think so,” said Norris. “I never really ever played GTA V, maybe a few times, but, yeah, I don’t have…I mean, it’s a cool game, and I enjoy almost what I watch other people playing and stuff like that, but, yeah, not my cup of tea. It’s awesome. “I would love to, but I wasn’t allowed to play it when I was younger. I wasn’t allowed, so when we would go on a school trip and I could nick someone else’s PSP or something, it was the best trip of my life because I could finally get to play it. “But I never grew up playing it when I was at home. I never really played it when I was older; therefore, it’s never been my thing. But I know a lot of people around the world are playing it right now, so maybe my mind changes, but for now, it’s a no.”

item.title: Is Arsenal’s attack weaker than it was last season?
item.description: Is Arsenal’s attack weaker than it was last season? Arsenal have established themselves among the strongest teams in Europe over recent seasons, with Mikel Arteta building a squad capable of delivering consistent performances. Since joining the club as manager at the end of 2019, the Spaniard has overseen a significant transformation and received continued backing from the board to implement his plans. The Gunners are now regarded as one of the best-run clubs in the Premier League and have assembled a squad capable of competing with leading sides across the continent. They will be determined to maintain that progress and remain among the strongest teams in the country. However, despite their achievements, Arsenal are facing a problem in front of goal. Their struggles to find the net have raised questions about the quality and depth of their attacking options, particularly as they approach another transfer window. Arsenal face questions over attacking options The Gunners have been linked with several strikers ahead of the January transfer window as they look to address their goalscoring concerns. A report from Football365 claims that Arteta’s attack has been worse this season than it was during the previous campaign. That assessment raises questions about the club’s decisions in the transfer market and whether their current options are providing enough attacking output. Arsenal have continued to rely on Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz as their main centre-forward options, but neither has scored as frequently as supporters would want. The club also signed Christos Tzolis , while maintaining their faith in Gyokeres and Havertz to lead the attack. However, the current situation suggests that Arsenal may need to consider further changes if they want to improve their goalscoring record. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) January transfer window could offer a solution The departures of Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli have also affected the attacking options available to Arteta. Losing those players leaves the manager with fewer choices in forward areas and increases the importance of finding suitable replacements. Arsenal will want to ensure that their attacking department can match the quality of the rest of their squad. Their reported interest in several strikers suggests they recognise the need to strengthen that area. The January transfer window could therefore provide an opportunity to address the problem. Arteta and the club’s recruitment team will need to assess their options carefully as they look to improve the team’s attacking output for the remainder of the season. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Fred Vasseur is running out of answers at Ferrari, says Jolyon Palmer
item.description: Motorsport photo In a 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix where 22 drivers traded a record 352 overtakes largely cleanly, Formula 1’s fiercest intra-team blowup still belonged to Ferrari . On Lap 38, Charles Leclerc dived down the inside of Lewis Hamilton at Turn 7 while battling over sixth place - tipping his team-mate into a spin, drawing a 10-second time penalty, and sparking a blunt post-race verdict from F1 TV analyst Jolyon Palmer . Asked why Ferrari’s pairing had come to blows yet again, Palmer did not hold back with his verdict. "Egos of drivers," Palmer said. "I mean, Charles clearly the aggressor there; Fred is pretty adamant where the blame lies. I said it on about Lap 10, when all the cars were fighting tooth and nail - what was it, 352 passes - and we were saying how good are the drivers being able to keep it clean. "And I just thought, 'You know who's not going to keep it clean? Somehow the one bit of contact will be between the two Ferraris.' And lo and behold, it does. Why? Because it always is. They race each other harder than they race anyone else." Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Reviewing the Turn 7 replay, Palmer noted that while Hamilton left tight room on the inside, Leclerc had no business gambling moments after receiving a direct team instruction. "Given he's just been warned by Ferrari a few corners before, it's an unnecessary risk to do that in that corner," Palmer said. "And they've got a complete disregard for the team. I feel a bit sorry for Fred because you just see him; he's worn out by trying to manage these two drivers. And I don't know what's next. You know, what more do you have to say?" Palmer’s sympathy followed a visibly exasperated trackside interview from Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur. Having already held stern clear-the-air talks after Leclerc took a five-second penalty for cutting across Hamilton on Lap 1 in Mexico City three weeks earlier, Vasseur did not mince words. "Honestly, my position is that once again, it's more than unacceptable," Vasseur told F1 TV. "I had exactly the same word after Mexico, but it's a lack of respect - it's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, but mainly for the people working at home. We passed the message to Charles five corners before, and for me it's a professional mistake." By Tuesday, Vasseur’s frustration had hardened further. Addressing the fallout ahead of Qatar, he admitted the internal pressure is "much worse now than it was 18 months ago", adding: "Lately, the situation between them has become unmanageable." item.description: Aaron Rodgers Slams Mike McCarthy For Falling Asleep In Meetings, More In Bizarre Interview originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . At 42 years old, Aaron Rodgers may not be a top NFL quarterback anymore. That isn't to say he isn't one of the most entertaining figures in the league, though. Rodgers was benched by the Steelers on Tuesday night, the team announced. And after reportedly being excused from Wednesday's practice, fans may have presumed they may not hear from the quarterback, who is likely in his last NFL season. Those fans were wrong. Rodgers, as he has many times in the past, appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" with very little filter on what went wrong with Pittsburgh over recent weeks, ripping into his longtime head coach, Mike McCarthy. Here's what Rodgers said in his appearance on McAfee's show. item.title: Five things Colorado football fans should know about the UCF Knights
item.description: Colorado will close out the regular season Saturday against UCF at Folsom Field, with kickoff at noon MT on TNT . The Knights are 6-5 overall and 4-4 in the Big 12 after beating Iowa State 48-17 on Nov. 20, clinching bowl eligibility for the first time since 2023. Colorado is 4-7 and 2-6 and has already been eliminated from bowl contention. Here are five things Colorado fans should know about UCF. 5. UCF is already bowl-eligible Head coach Scott Frost said the victory over Iowa State was probably the Knights' most complete game of the season. He also said he doesn't know whether UCF has played two strong games in a row this year, and he sees Saturday as a chance to find that consistency. "Sometimes you're dangerous when you don't have anything to lose and you just go play hard," Frost said when asked about Colorado. 4. Scott Frost is in the second year of his return Frost came back to UCF before the 2025 season after leading the Knights to a 13-0 record in 2017. UCF averages 30.2 points per game this season and has allowed 25.2. He is 4-1 in Boulder as a player, assistant coach and head coach. Frost beat Colorado 27-24 as Nebraska's quarterback in 1997, won three games in Boulder with Oregon, and lost 34-31 in overtime in 2019 as Nebraska's head coach. His career record against Colorado is 7-2. 3. Alonza Barnett III is playing his best football Barnett was named to the Davey O'Brien Great 8 and a Manning Star of the Week after Iowa State. He completed 17 of 27 passes for 255 yards and four touchdowns and ran for 43 yards and a score. He has thrown for at least 250 yards in each of his three starts since returning from injury, and UCF scored on its first four possessions against Iowa State. 2. Duke Watson and Josh Derry lead the skill players Running back Duke Watson averages more than 6.3 yards per carry and has more than 700 rushing yards. He gained 113 yards against Iowa State. Wide receiver Josh Derry has 56 catches for 833 yards and seven touchdowns and scored three times last week, including touchdown receptions of 21 and 65 yards. Frost called Watson "one of my favorite guys," saying he "runs really tough." 1. UCF has beaten elite teams and also lost badly UCF upset No. 2 BYU 39-31 in October and won 33-32 at Kansas on a final-second play. The Knights also lost 41-9 to Baylor and 26-13 to Arizona State at home and are 1-3 on the road. Frost described the season as a roller coaster. item.title: Romeo Doubs returns to Patriots practice ahead of Chargers game
item.description: Another member of the New England Patriots starting offense has returned to practice. Two days after left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker , wide receiver Romeo Doubs made his comeback on Wednesday. His participation at practice indicates that the Patriots have opened his 21-day window to be activated from injured reserve to the 53-man roster. WR Romeo Doubs returned to practice Wednesday, opening his 21-day activation window. pic.twitter.com/ZjaoEHDLG5 — Brian Hines (@iambrianhines) November 25, 2026 Doubs, 26, missed the last four games on injured reserve because of a shoulder ailment he suffered on a touchdown catch in Week 6 against the New York Jets. A former member of the Green Bay Packers, Doubs arrived in New England in March on a four-year, $68 million free agency deal. Before hurting his shoulder early in is sixth game, he had caught 14 passes for 261 yards and three touchdowns. He also had been on the field for 68.2% of the Patriots’ offensive snaps by the time he went down. Doubs’ return means that he, like the aforementioned Alijah Vera-Tucker, is now eligible to appear in this week’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers. item.title: ‘1,2,3 Packers’: Aaron Rodgers details baffling Mike McCarthy halftime moment
item.description: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images In one of the craziest on-screen interviews you’ll ever see the current quarterback of a football team give, Aaron Rodgers went scorched earth on things that have been happening behind the scenes with the Pittsburgh Steelers. One of the most bizarre quotes from Rodgers’ sit-down on The Pat McAfee Show was his recount of how McCarthy broke down the huddle at halftime. Rodgers says McCarthy said “one, two, three, Packers” to close the halftime huddle. Alan Saunders of Steelers Now says that a player confirmed to him that this was true. “I can confirm that this happened,” Saunders wrote on X . “I had been told about this by another player who asked me not to share it.” This was just one of a laundry list of things Rodgers had to say about McCarthy, which also included: Sleeping in team meetings, not watching film, not knowing the game plan and call sheet, and not making an effort to get to know defensive players. The preemptive move comes as the current labor deal is set to expire in less than a week. The filing in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York seeks to block the union from dissolving under what is called “disclaiming”. Under such a scenario, without union representation under labor law, one or more players could sue the league on antitrust grounds. The league is filing ahead of the expiration of the current labor deal on Dec. 1 at 11:59 pm E.T., claiming there is a past history of union leadership and Jeffery Kessler, who is outside counsel, doing so. Bruce Meyer, the interim head of the MLB Players’ Association, was with the NHLPA prior. item.title: Derrick White on navigating changing roles over time with Boston Celtics
item.description: Derrick White has known the struggle of trying to carve out a niche in the NBA. And he is well-versed in how to be a key cog in a contending ball club. Now he is starting to transition toward the end of his prime years in the league, comparting his experience to a new generation of teammates while adapting his game to reflect what the Boston Celtics need from him that he can provide consistently. "When you're a young guy, you're just trying to figure out how to stay in the league," explained White on a recent episode of the team-produced "View from the Rafters" podcast. "Just trying to figure out if you belong, you're trying to figure out what makes you successful. So you're trying to figure all of that out and learn as much as you can and (to) try to be a sponge." "And then I think now, I've been in this my 10th year, so (I've) been in highs and lows," he added. "I've seen pretty much every game, and so nothing surprises me as when I was like young." "It's always a good reminder of guys like (Paul George) and (Mike Conley) that have had unbelievable careers and done so many amazing things in the league, but how hard it is to win a championship and how many guys are still reaching there or trying to get that goal," said White. "So that's always a good reminder. I remember when (Al Horford) hadn't won one, and we all wanted to push it for Al. So now it's like Mike and PG, they've had amazing careers that we want to help them get something they never done before." item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
